title: Task Management Software Comparison for Teams
description: A comparison of task management platforms including Todoist, Asana, ClickUp, Microsoft To Do, and Things 3, evaluating features, workflows, and suitability for different team sizes.
body:
Task management software helps individuals and teams organize work, track progress, and meet deadlines. The category spans simple personal to-do lists through enterprise project management platforms, with pricing and features varying accordingly.

This comparison evaluates five task management platforms across feature depth, workflow flexibility, collaboration capabilities, and pricing. All pricing references should be verified against each vendor's current rates.

## Todoist

Todoist is the most popular dedicated task management application, known for its speed, simplicity, and cross-platform availability. Its natural language date parsing enables rapid task entry across devices.

Todoist organizes tasks with projects, sections, labels, and filters. The priority system uses four levels to distinguish urgency. Productivity tracking features include karma points, daily and weekly goals, and completion trends.

Todoist's free plan supports basic task management for individuals. Paid plans add labels, filters, reminders, and team collaboration features.

Check Todoist's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Asana

Asana serves teams that need structured project management alongside task tracking. Its multiple view options support list, board, timeline, calendar, and Gantt chart representations of work.

Asana's key strength is its project management depth. Tasks can include subtasks, dependencies, custom fields, and attachments. Workflow automation rules trigger actions based on task status changes, reducing manual process management.

Asana's free plan supports basic task management for small teams. Paid plans add timeline view, advanced reporting, workflow automation, and portfolio management.

Check Asana's current pricing page for exact rates.

## ClickUp

ClickUp positions itself as an all-in-one productivity platform combining task management, document collaboration, goal tracking, and time tracking. Its customizable workspace adapts to different work styles and team structures.

ClickUp's flexibility is both a strength and a weakness. The platform supports more configuration options than any competitor, making it adaptable to almost any workflow. However, the initial setup and learning curve can be significant.

ClickUp's free plan provides generous features for individuals and small teams. Paid plans add advanced automation, timelines, and reporting capabilities.

Check ClickUp's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Microsoft To Do

Microsoft To Do is a lightweight task management application integrated with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. Its simplicity makes it ideal for personal task management and basic team coordination.

Microsoft To Do integrates with Outlook tasks, Microsoft Planner, and Microsoft Teams. Tasks created in any Microsoft application sync across the suite, providing unified task visibility for Microsoft-centric organizations.

Microsoft To Do is free with a Microsoft account or included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions. Its capabilities are limited compared to dedicated task management platforms.

## Things 3

Things 3 is a premium task management application available exclusively on Apple devices. Its design philosophy emphasizes focus and intentional task management through a structured workflow.

Things 3 organizes tasks into an area, project, and heading hierarchy. The today view surfaces tasks scheduled for the current day alongside upcoming deadlines. The review feature encourages regular task list maintenance.

Things 3 uses a one-time purchase pricing model rather than subscription. The Mac, iPhone, and iPad versions are sold separately as individual purchases.

Check Things 3's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Selection Guidance

The right task management platform depends on team size, workflow complexity, and existing tool ecosystem. Todoist is best for individuals and small teams who want speed and simplicity. Asana serves teams with structured project management needs. ClickUp offers maximum configurability for organizations that need an all-in-one platform. Microsoft To Do is ideal for Microsoft 365 users. Things 3 serves Apple-focused users who prefer one-time purchases over subscriptions.
